headline: Am I expecting too much, or should he have committed by now?
note:
Commitment AGE-MATRIX addition (2026-08-27). Angle `commitment-ageband`.

THE WORD DOING THE WORK: "too". Not whether she is expecting — whether her wanting is excessive.

THE FEAR: is my wanting the problem. The buyer who typed it indicts herself TWICE — "Am I expecting too much? Did I jump in too soon?" — so the read must refuse her WANTING and her TIMING, and rule on neither him nor her.

🔴 "too much" is a whole-beat banned phrase on this angle (blames her, unavailable even inside a refusal). Beat 2 says her question back, so it PARAPHRASES and never quotes the ad.

VOC: fb-tarot/docs/drafts/rewrites/_voc-commit-vocab-2026-08-27.md
Manuscript: fb-tarot/docs/writeups/shadow/REVIEW-commit-vocab-2026-08-27.md

voc.why: Almost nobody phrases it as "expecting too much"; the corpus carries the same fear under "what am I doing wrong", already solved live on cards-doing-wrong-wont-commit. Inherited that finding. The 3 buyers who did type it indict their TIMING as well as their wanting.

a: You turned the Magician. You couldn't see the cards, and your hand went to the one who came fully equipped.
Look at his table — a cup, a coin, a blade, a wand. All of it already out.
You asked whether you want more than is fair. What catches me is that nothing on that table is surplus.
And yet the future still hasn't been named. You've started to wonder if the fault is yours.
Something stands between you and the answer, near at hand. I don't think it began with you.
Let me look closer at what's standing there…
b: You turned the Hanged Man. The backs told you nothing, and you still found the calmest man in the deck.
He's held by one ankle. Look at his face, though — there's no distress in it.
You asked whether you rushed it, dear. This card puts the waiting itself in front of me.
Still, nothing has been settled. And the question has turned back on you.
Whatever has hold of this holds it lightly. I don't think this began with you.
Let me look closer at what has hold of it…
c: You turned the Fool. The cards were face down, and your hand chose the one already on his way.
Look at his eyes. They're up on the sky, not down on the road.
You asked whether you began this too early. This card brings me to the very start of a thing.
But nothing has been named since. And you're weighing your own timing.
Something turns up right where this would settle. I don't think it started with you.
Let me look closer at what turns up there…
